text:
Seoul shares opened sharply lower Friday, tracking losses on Wall Street, as Anthropic's solid market debut failed to ease concerns over whether heavy investment in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure will generate returns.
After opening 4.08 percent lower, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) fell 183.50 points, or 3.57 percent, to 4,954.39 as of 9:15 a.m.
Overnight, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 2.19 percent, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq composite declined 2.25 percent.
Investors are awaiting further evidence that heavy investment in the AI sector will generate sustainable returns, despite Anthropic's successful market debut.
Shares in Anthropic soared 17 percent above their initial public offering (IPO) price of $83 to close at $97.17 on Thursday (U.S. time) on Wall Street.
But the biggest IPO ever was not enough to alleviate woes over the AI sector and its related segment.
Market bellwether Samsung Electronics fell 4.22 percent, while its chipmaking rival SK hynix declined 5.75 percent.
Top carmaker Hyundai Motor dropped 2.06 percent, and national flag carrier Korean Air shed 2 percent.
Among gainers, Korea Aerospace Industries, the country's sole aircraft manufacturer, rose 0.1 percent and leading budget carrier Jeju Air climbed 0.96 percent.
The Korean won was quoted at 1,336.15 won against the U.S. dollar as of 9:15 a.m., down 2.05 won from the previous trading session's close.
